source.title: Dissociable stages of human memory consolidation and reconsolidation.

confidence_rationale: Supports the abstract dissociation MECH-476 asserts (acquisition, consolidation, and reconsolidation are separable stages with distinct substrate requirements) and independently corroborates the interference-resistance definition. But it simultaneously localises biological consolidation to SLEEP and shows reactivation returns a memory to a labile state -- both of which REE lacks. It is therefore the clearest single marker of the known AWAKE/ONLINE/UNDIFFERENTIATED-vs-sleep/replay divergence, which is why it is filed as mixed rather than supports.
failure_signatures: The consolidation that matters here is time-in-SLEEP, not merely elapsed clock time -- overnight sleep produced consolidation that equivalent waking time did not. REE's demonstrated protection pathways (distributional critic, KL anchor) are awake/online and have no sleep or replay analog, so a REE interval effect driven purely by offline STEPS is not the same object Walker measured, and a null REE interval effect does not falsify the biological process.

Waking reactivation turned a previously consolidated memory back into a labile, interference-susceptible state (reconsolidation). REE has no reactivation-gated labile window, so its retention dynamics may be strictly monotone where biology's are cyclic -- a structural mismatch the claim should not paper over.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Human motor-skill (finger-tapping) memory passes through at least three dissociable post-acquisition stages. Wake and sleep make distinct contributions to consolidation, and waking reactivation of a consolidated memory returns it to a labile state that then requires reconsolidation.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-476's core structural assertion that acquisition and retention are separable capabilities served by distinct processes -- Walker shows the post-acquisition timeline is itself multi-stage, not a single strengthening. But it pins the biological consolidation stage to sleep and adds a reactivation-labile stage REE does not have, making it the reference for the divergence MECH-476 records: REE's protection is awake, online, and trace-undifferentiated.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Do not read Walker as licensing a REE offline-INTERVAL effect. His interval that mattered was time-asleep, not time-elapsed; equivalent waking time did not consolidate. REE's offline 'interval' is idle/offline optimisation steps with no sleep-stage structure, so a positive REE interval effect would be a WEAKER, mechanism-divergent analog, and a negative one would not contradict Walker. The reconsolidation finding has no current REE analog at all.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans; sequential finger-tapping motor skill; overnight sleep vs equivalent waking retention intervals; reactivation-then-interference manipulation.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality Nature study, robust and much-replicated. But its central mechanistic content (sleep-dependence, reactivation-lability) is exactly what REE lacks, so mapping_fidelity and transfer_risk both pull confidence down. Filed mixed and at 0.6 because its value is dual: it corroborates the dissociation framing while defining the boundary of the transfer.
